senses.gloss:
Saguṇa-Brahman
(‘Brahman with qualities’)
------------------------------------------
See ADVAITA VEDĀNTA DARŚANA.

sagotra
(‘of the same गोत्र or lineage’)
------------------------------------------
The words गोत्र and प्रवर have been used extensively in the smṛtis and धर्मशास्त्रस्.
Sagotra means a person belonging to the same गोत्र. Marriages between persons of the same गोत्र have been prohibited.
See GOTRA for details.

sagarbha
(‘with the womb [of the मन्त्र]’)
------------------------------------------
See NIRGARBHA.

Sagara
(‘one [who was born] with poison’)
------------------------------------------
Sagara was a king of the सूर्य-vaṁśa (solar race). He was the son of king बाहुक and Yādavī.
Bāhuka was a moral wreck and hence had been conquered by Tālajaṅgha, the king of the Haihayas. When he went to the forest and started living there, his first wife Yādavī was pregnant. His second wife had administered gara or poison to her without her knowledge. This prevented Yādavī from giving birth to her child, for seven years! Meanwhile बाहुक died of old age. When Yādavī wanted to die on his funeral pyre, the sage और्व भार्गव, prevented it and brought her to his own hermitage. Due to the holy atmosphere of the hermitage, she gave birth to a baby-boy who was named ‘Sagara’ (one who was born with or in spite of, gara or poison) by the sage.
When सगर grew up into a fine young man, well-trained by और्व भार्गव in all arts and sciences, he learnt about the tragedy that had befallen his ड़थेर् बाहुक. He then built up an army, raided अयोध्या, defeated Tālajaṅgha and regained his paternal kingdom. He ruled the kingdom very well for several years.
He had sixty-thousand sons from his wife Vaidarbhī and one son Asamañja from his second wife Śaibyā.
Asamañja proved to be a rogue and was banished by the ड़थेर्.
When सगर performed the अश्वमेध sacrifice, the horse was stolen by इन्द्र (the king of gods), who left it in the hermitage of the great sage कपिल, in the पाताल-लोक or nether world. सगर’s sixty thousand sons while searching for the missing horse, dug up the earth up to the पाताल, found the horse, but incurred the displeasure of the sage कपिल and were reduced to ashes.
When the king भगीरथ, a descendent of सगर brought the river गङ्गा to the earth, to save his ancestors, this huge pit was filled up and became the ocean, called ‘sāgara’ derived from ‘Sagara’.
Sagara spent his last days in the आश्रम of और्व भार्गव.
See also BHAGĪRATHA.
